title: [Bugfix][MiniMax-M3] Guard sparse decode sentinel indices
body:
## Purpose

MiniMax-M3's Triton split-K sparse decode can receive `-1` in unused
`topk_idx` entries. Triton treats `bt_row + blk` as raw pointer arithmetic, so
an unguarded `blk == -1` reads immediately before the request's block-table row
and can form an invalid KV-cache pointer.

This change makes the kernel safe independently of the top-k producer:

- Map negative or out-of-range logical blocks to safe block 0 before reading
  the block table.
- Mask their K/V loads and make them a neutral online-softmax update.
- Keep the loop branch-free so valid decode rows retain a pipeline-friendly
  load/dot structure.

The upper-bound guard does not change a valid contribution: the decode loop
uses `num_blocks = ceil(kv_len / 128)`, so a logical block at or above that
bound starts at or beyond `kv_len` and was already fully excluded by the
position mask. The guard only prevents dereferencing a block whose numerical
contribution was already zero.

The producer-side FULL dummy-metadata correction is intentionally excluded
from this PR and is reviewed separately in #54604.

I searched open vLLM issues and PRs for this failure and found no existing fix.
#49054 handles empty-row merge NaNs, while #52060 optimizes scalar KV scales;
neither guards the block-table dereference.

This is an AI-assisted contribution. OpenAI Codex provided non-trivial
assistance with the implementation and tests. The human submitter is
responsible for reviewing the changed lines and validation results.

## Test Plan

- Use two contiguous block-table rows so request 1's raw `-1` offset resolves
  deterministically to the final element of request 0's row.
- Poison that exact element with an out-of-range physical page.
- Exercise one valid block followed by 15 sentinels with four query tokens and
  a long sequence.
- Cover both supported KV layouts, eager execution, CUDA graph capture, and
  three graph replays.
- Compare finite output against the existing sparse-attention reference while
  retaining the existing all-valid decode/reference tests.
- Run negative-control reproductions in a dedicated process because the
  expected illegal access leaves the CUDA context unusable.
- Measure all-valid decode latency before marking the PR ready.

## Test Result

- All changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX,
  forbidden-import, and CUDA-API checks.
- Python bytecode compilation and `git diff --check` passed.
- GPU negative-control, fixed-kernel, and latency measurements are pending.
